name: Malachite-Ruin
description: Malachite-Ruin takes its name from the vivid green copper-carbonate deposits that streak its canyon walls like veins in aged marble. The planet's surface tells the story of a world that once held oceans; dry basins stretch for hundreds of kilometers, their floors cracked and pale, bordered by petrified forests of unknown species. A thin atmosphere clings to the lower elevations, just enough to carry fine dust on a whisper of wind.

Walking the canyon floors feels like moving through the bones of a dead world. The green-stained walls tower overhead, and petrified trunks cast long shadows in the dim light of a distant orange star. The thin air carries no scent, but the silence has a quality of expectation, as though the planet is holding its breath.

The ruins emerged from erosion over centuries, geometric structures half-buried in the canyon walls that predate any known spacefaring civilization. Deeper scans revealed a megastructure beneath the largest basin, its purpose unknown, its scale suggesting a species that thought in terms of continents. The microbial life clinging to existence in subsurface moisture pockets may be the last echo of whatever biosphere once flourished here.

Archaeological expeditions have mapped only a fraction of the buried structure, and funding is perpetually contested between those who want to excavate and those who fear disturbing something best left alone. The microbes are genetically unlike anything in existing databases, raising the possibility that they were engineered rather than evolved. Malachite-Ruin holds answers to questions no one has thought to ask yet.
